newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open flat, shrugs off lower GDP.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open flat, shrugs off lower GDP.

text.p: Singapore's share market on Wednesday was flat as investors shrugged off the government's overnight announcement of a poorer third quarter economic performance and again revised down its 1996 growth projection, dealers said.
At 0215 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was a mere 0.79 point off at 2,069.44. Market turnover was meagre, around 19 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 82 to 43.
"A weak Gross Domestic Product has already been factored in by fund managers. So it doesn't matter if the government shaves off half or one percent from its projection," a dealer said.

Late Tuesday, Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said third quarter growth was 3.2 percent against second quarter's 7.5 percent and lowered 1996 growth forecast to about six percent against a projection of 7.0-8.0 percent made in August.
Dealers said results of the U.S. presidential election was inconsequential to the Singapore bourse.

Activity in the morning was dominated by block deals. These include UIC Ltd, which saw 800,000 shares crossed at Singapore $1.18 (US$0.84) each, CM Telecom had 742,000 shares crossed at S$0.265 and Uraco saw a block deal of 600,000 shares at S$0.80-0.81. Creative Technology fell S$0.30.
